title: Global Optimality of Midori Cell Permutations
summary: Restricted searches find optimal Midori cell permutations only within row-based and row/column-based classes; global optimality over all 16!

formal_statement.body: For the Midori block cipher's almost-MDS diffusion layer, determine whether a globally optimal permutation of the 16 cells in its $4\times 4$ state exists or can be characterized among all $16!$ cell permutations, where optimality means maximizing the minimum number of active S-boxes and minimizing the number of diffusion rounds. The available search restricts permutations to reduced row-based and row/column-based classes, identifying optima only within those classes and not establishing global optimality over all $16!$ permutations. The unresolved task is therefore to construct or characterize a globally optimal cell permutation under these criteria.

scope.domain: Lightweight block-cipher design, specifically cell permutations for Midori's almost-MDS diffusion layer.
parameters: 16 cells in a 4-by-4 state—the permutation domain
Minimum number of active S-boxes—the quantity to maximize
Number of diffusion rounds—the quantity to minimize
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct or characterize a globally optimal cell permutation among all 16! possibilities under the active-S-box and diffusion-round criteria.

citations.label: Midori: A Block Cipher for Low Energy

progress.summary: The source reports that exhaustively evaluating all 16! permutations is computationally hard, so it searches reduced row-based and row/column-based classes. It identifies optima within those classes but does not establish global optimality.
citation_labels: Subhadeep Banik et al., Midori: A Block Cipher for Low Energy
